  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 12:40 p.m. for Closed Session and 1:30 p.m. for Open
Session. Please be mindful that seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
 comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities A
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contact
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280,  FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester
Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

Inglewood, California
  June 25, 2024

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
June 25, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:02 p.m.

The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor Butts, Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk;
  and
  Absent: None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager
  Christine Padilla  Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
of 2:02 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Derald Brenneman  Acting City Attorney/Acting General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PRESENTATION. This presentation was postponed to a later date.

Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
on the Agendas.

There was no response.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Brandie Keith, Outreach Team for South Coast Air Quality Management District
  Representative, introduced herself and stated that she represented the South Bay. She noted
  that wildfire season was coming and wanted to raise awareness regarding the effects of air
  quality on your health, even miles away. Brandie also stated that their website had resources
  available to check the current air quality and tips for protecting your health before, after,
  and during a wildfire crisis. Finally, she mentioned signing up to receive air quality alerts
  and provided their web address.

  Scott Schwatzski, a long-time resident of Inglewood, raised concerns about parking issues
  during stadium events. He mentioned that parking during events is a major problem for his
  tenants as well as their guests, as there is not enough space to park on the streets. He also
  noted instances where guests had to double park in the building's driveway, which led to
  difficulties for emergency vehicles to pass through. Scott expressed the need for
  implementing changes to ensure that people park at the stadium instead. He recounted an
  instance when he went to City Hall on a Monday and found no parking available due to
  Monday Night Football. Scott emphasized the urgent need for change to address these
  parking issues.
